name: Giddel
overview: Giddel is a male member of the tribe of Levi who served as a temple servant. His role as a temple servant highlights his participation in the sacred duties associated with the worship and service of God in the temple. There are no additional notes provided about his life or activities.
namesAndTitles: The name Giddel means 'big' and is a proper name mentioned in Ezra 2:47. There is no indication that the name was given by God, and no additional titles are associated with him.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Giddel is a descendant of Levi, linking him to the Levitical lineage responsible for temple service. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no further family relationships are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Giddel's significance lies in his role as a Levitical temple servant, underscoring the importance of faithful service in the post-exilic community's worship life. His mention in Ezra 2:47 situates him among those who returned to Jerusalem and contributed to the restoration of temple worship. Though details are sparse, his inclusion reflects the continuity of Levitical duties in God's redemptive plan.
